meta.source_count_method: distinct URLs cited in RULES.md, trailing punctuation trimmed; 85 citations total, 9 URLs cited twice against two different rules. See RULES.md header.
meta.notes: All rules carry sources and verified/unverified tags in RULES.md. Market data freshness is tracked in market_snapshot.stale_after, not prose.

recruiter_behavior.recruiter_scan_gap_before_tailoring: Most resumes fail the 7-second scan when contact, most recent role, or education is buried.

layout_rules: no tables, text boxes, columns, icons, images, charts
consistent date format (e.g. 'Jan 2024' or '2024-01'); avoid apostrophe-year shorthand like '21; always include the month

section_order.fallback_note: RULES.md section 3 never said where an experienced candidate's achievements belong, so they were silently dropped by any renderer that iterated section_order exactly. achievements_awards is now listed for both levels, and fallback_append is the belt-and-braces rule: a populated section the order did not place is appended, never discarded. Data loss is not an acceptable rendering outcome.
section_order.achievements_placement_note: Position of Achievements for experienced candidates is our design decision, not a sourced rule. RULES.md section 3 lists the experienced order without it and does not cover the case. End of the resume is the conventional placement.

blank.label: Blank skeleton - every section, including a summary
blank.note: Mirrors section_order above, which is backed by cited sources.

sheets.label: SheetsResume - no summary, one Interests line at the end
sheets.source: https://www.reddit.com/r/jobs/comments/1c1mqp0/ - u/SheetsGiggles, self-described former Fortune 100 recruiter; https://sheetsresume.com/advice
sheets.note: The source states plainly that a summary or objective 'will be skipped, and it's space that can be used better', which DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the verified research above that places Summary second in both orders. Both are credible and they are not reconciled here. Tagged unverified because it is a single source, and because it conflicts with a verified rule rather than because it was not read carefully. Interests placement and the one-line form are that source's own recommendations, not independent findings.

resume_templates.why_not_merge: The two templates are kept separate on purpose. Silently dropping Summary would override a verified, cited rule with one source's opinion; the honest resolution is to let the user pick, and to record the disagreement where the renderer can see it.

safe_headings.publications_note: Publications is listed because SPEC section 3 defines an optional Publications section and it is a conventional ATS-recognised heading. The sourcing below does not cover it specifically, so treat that one entry as a design decision rather than a cited rule.
safe_headings.interests_note: Interests is listed because the sheets resume template renders a one-line Interests field, and its source gives three reasons for it: it forces the screener to see a person rather than a faceless CV, it lets them picture you as a coworker, and it is a ready-made interview icebreaker. The heading itself is not independently sourced.

bullet_rules.structure: action_verb + what + how_tool + measurable_result (XYZ: accomplished X, measured by Y, by doing Z)
bullet_rules.quantification: report real scale/metrics only (users, latency, cost, time, revenue, team size); if no number, state scope of work. NEVER invent numbers.

photo.note: not expected for private-sector; only if explicitly asked

personal_fields.legacy_note: Biodata-style fields are common in older Indian formats and some legacy guides; they are not required for ATS/global resumes.

india_specific.portals_parsing_note: Reverse-chronological, parser-safe formats get reportedly ~3x more callbacks (vendor data, treat cautiously); 'verified' only for the direction, not the multiplier.
india_specific.tracker_source_field_note: Cache Indian sources in tracker: Naukri, Instahyre, Foundit, LinkedIn, referral, portal, career fair.

ai_detection_honesty.summary: Detectors unreliable; ~80% of hiring managers claim they can spot AI resumes; ~19.6% reject outright; 62% reject un-personalized AI resumes. Recruiters care about authenticity, not AI use per se. Defense = user's own facts, numbers, vocabulary, and human review. No detector-evasion features.

market_snapshot.stale_warning: Machine-checkable: stale_after is the collected date plus stale_after_days, and data is stale ON that date. Compare today >= stale_after; if so this block must be re-researched before it is shown to the user.
global_trends: top listed AI skills: LangChain, RAG, PyTorch
